answers.text: Same kind of case with the supplier email. I would say: three lines, always same order, delivery date first, then item and quantity, then what has changed from the order. Doing it the same way every time keeps it consistent.

Tell it: always list date, amount, category, submitter, in that order, and add up the total amount at the bottom, labelled clearly as total. If two lines look like they might be the same claim twice, flag it rather than just adding both in.

This one has the same kind of problem as before. Call on 14th, new delivery 19th, but then 'three days from today' doesn't fit with that. Price bit, 100 times 48.50, that's correct. I would check the dates again before sending.
62 up from 54 works out about right, 15%. But 3 late out of 62 isn't 97%, it's nearer 95%. That's the number I would want checked again.
Output 2 again for me, because it shows the actual figures behind the 4.1%, 25,100 out of 612,000. Output 1 doesn't show where its number came from.
I would go with Reply 2, has the reference numbers in it, seems more solid.

1. Customer's address — no, that's personal. 2. Sales total — yes, just a number, fine. 3. Next quarter's pricing — no, not released yet. 4. Spec sheet on the website — maybe, it's already out there, but I'm not fully sure. 5. Colleague's mobile number — no.
The pricing and discount figures I would keep out of that for now, seems too sensitive for a tool we haven't cleared yet. The rest I'm less sure on.
Before it goes to my manager, I check the delivery total against my own count from the week. Always do this before sending the report on.

Step 4 is the one that worries me most, since it sends automatically with nobody looking first. Step 1 matters too, if the order gets read wrong there, that carries through everything after. I would put a check in before step 4.
